Liam West: Heads-up — ran into a nasty streaming-onboarding bug in the sampleapp where very fast reconnects + heartbeat lines produce duplicate or truncated final deltas. Repro on Android webview polyfill.
Noah Park: ugh. quick repro steps?
Liam West: 1) start sampleapp streaming demo 2) server streams small tokenized deltas and sends a keepalive ':' heartbeat between chunks 3) force a 100ms network flap right when server is mid-write 4) client reconnects immediately -> sometimes we see duplicate final delta or final delta split and never applied.
Anya S.: interesting — heartbeats can cause an empty-line flush in some parsers. Do you have raw framing?
Liam West: pasted raw capture (trimmed):
```
:data

# main chunk starts
data: {"id":"d-512","part":1,"text":"hel"

# heartbeat emitted by server
:

# network drop ~100ms -> reconnect
> GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood
> Last-Event-ID: d-512

# server logs: resumed, replayed buffered partial, client later receives remaining part -> ends up with duplicate/partial apply
```
sdk-bot: Known class of issues: parser flush-on-empty-line + immediate reconnect can re-enqueue buffered partials if resume detection misses canonical header.
Noah Park: two vectors here: 1) header parity/casing across sdks/proxies 2) parser semantics around heartbeats and mid-event EOF. Also some mobile polyfills send lowercase 'last-event-id' only.
Liam West: observed node SDK sets both 'Last-Event-ID' and 'X-Last-Event-Id', python/mobile often only send lowercase header. Envoy lowercases when buffering; our resume check in the router currently looks for "Last-Event-Id" canonical only which means a miss can cause replay.
Anya S.: short-term mitigations: - normalize resume header in router middleware (map any-case to canonical Last-Event-Id) - make resume application idempotent by deduping on event-id at apply time - tweak parser to not treat a single heartbeat newline as finalization for a currently-open multi-line data block.
Noah Park: long-term: SDK parity: add small helper that sets both canonical + lowercase resume headers on reconnect, and add optional "sse-resume-id" custom header that's less likely to be touched by proxies. Document in SDK onboarding.
Liam West: agreed. Also adding a tiny reconnect backoff jitter (100-300ms) in sampleapp demo greatly reduces hit-rate of the race during onboarding. We'll add as a default in demo code so new integrators don't trip.
Anya S.: tests: suggest an e2e that uses a raw TCP stub server to emit a split final chunk with an intermediate heartbeat, then kill connection and reconnect with/without auth-refresh; assert exactly one final application of id d-512. Add flaky marker and run under sampleapp CI.
Noah Park: I'll open router PR for header normalization + unit for parser heartbeat behavior. Liam, can you send a small PR to sampleapp to add jitter + dual header set? Add a line to SDK changelog about canonical header + sse-resume-id.
Liam West: PRs opened: sampleapp/#304 (jitter + dual header), platform/router/#659 (normalize header). ci triggered.
devops-bot: build 9981 queued for sampleapp/#304.
Anya S.: follow-up doc: quick blurb in SDK onboarding FAQ describing polyfill differences, heartbeat effects, and recommended reconnect jitter to reduce this class of issues. I'll draft it after PRs merge. :memo:
